description:
The Cima was built for the climb that never stops. Now it carries the material that started it all.

At the core of the Cima TC is a refined Tri-Composite weave: carbon fiber interlaced with copper filament, tightened to a finer pattern than before. The result is a surface that holds more consistency under stress, with the same signature depth of finish that made the original Raso TC unmistakable.

The Cima TC brings together two things Sarto has spent decades perfecting. From the Cima: the endurance-inspired geometry, the race-oriented handling, the diamond profile at the head tube and down tube. From Tri-Composite: a carbon structure reinforced with metallic filament, built to absorb road vibration and resist impact without adding weight.

Every tube is still hand-laminated. Every joint is still hand-wrapped and bonded, tube-to-tube, in the Pianiga workshop. Nothing about the process changed. What changed is what the process now produces.

Tri-Composite carbon does two jobs at once: it damps vibration through the frame, and it holds its stiffness where the frame needs to stay precise. On the Cima TC, that means a bike that climbs like a race bike and rides all day like an endurance bike, exactly the balance the Cima was designed around from the start.

The Cima TC launches in Blue, Green, Red, and White. Each filament color runs through the Tri-Composite weave itself, not just the paint, so the effect shifts with the light and holds up over years, not seasons.
